name: Japan
hook: Shinto, the shogun and Mount Fuji: Japan's clues reward knowing the old titles and the new emperors.

facts.label: Shinto
facts.statement: Shinto, Japan's native religion, means "the way of the gods"; its name comes from Chinese words.

facts.label: Mount Fuji
facts.statement: Mount Fuji is Japan's sacred peak; Hokusai's Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji made it famous, and some Buddhists treat the 33rd and 88th ascents as special.

facts.label: Kyoto
facts.statement: Kyoto, called Heian-Kyo, became Japan's capital in 794 under Emperor Kammu; the Kansai dialect is spoken there and in Osaka.

facts.label: shogun
facts.statement: Shogun means "great general"; Yoritomo received the title in 1192, and James Clavell's 1975 novel Shogun is set in Japan in 1600.

facts.label: Emperor Hirohito
facts.statement: Emperor Hirohito died in 1989 after more than 60 years on the throne; he was buried with a Mickey Mouse watch and succeeded by Akihito.

facts.label: kabuki
facts.statement: Kabuki is a highly stylized Japanese drama; the Nakamura-za was a leading venue, and Sharaku made prints of its actors.

facts.label: Okinawa
facts.statement: Okinawa, the largest Ryukyu island, takes its name from Japanese for "rope in the sea" and was returned to Japan in 1972.
